cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 010
title: multi
status: queued
depends_on: 001 002 003
---
body
' > factory/specs/010-a.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; tracker_dep_drop factory/specs/010-a.md 002; AFTER_DROP="$(_tracker_field factory/specs/010-a.md depends_on)"; tracker_dep_replace factory/specs/010-a.md 003 007; AFTER_REP="$(_tracker_field factory/specs/010-a.md depends_on)"; if ( tracker_dep_replace factory/specs/010-a.md 099 100 ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then MISS=0; else MISS=$?; fi; UNCHANGED="$(_tracker_field factory/specs/010-a.md depends_on)"; tracker_dep_drop factory/specs/010-a.md 001; tracker_dep_drop factory/specs/010-a.md 007; EMPTY="$(_tracker_field factory/specs/010-a.md depends_on)"; jq -n --arg d "$AFTER_DROP" --arg r "$AFTER_REP" --argjson m "$MISS" --arg u "$UNCHANGED" --arg e "$EMPTY" '{drop: $d, rep: $r, miss: $m, unchanged: $u, empty: $e}'
_note: dep-replace on an id that is not there must FAIL rather than no-op: a silent no-op reads as a successful rewire, and the user walks away believing a chain was repaired when it was not. Dropping the last dependency must leave the field empty, not a stale list.
